summary: Stone tower of 1829-1830 on a tidal islet where the St. Lawrence estuary meets the Gulf; a Fafard family station for 82 years, now a museum open to climb.

lens.note: Seventeen Argand lamps with parabolic reflectors at first; triple-flashing catoptric apparatus from 1914 (LighthouseFriends).

access.note: Open to visitors. Reached by a wooden bridge of about 200 m; the tower stands on an island at high tide (LighthouseFriends).

stay.note: Four guest rooms in the keeper's dwelling, with a restaurant on the ground floor (LighthouseFriends).

facts.agency: Québec Ministère de la Culture et des Communications (owner); Corporation du Phare de Pointe-des-Monts (manager)

events.note: Construction began in July 1829 (LighthouseFriends). Register: construction 1829-1830.
Light first shown 20 September 1830 (LighthouseFriends; register 92571 gives the same date).
Provision depot for shipwreck survivors added the year after the light was first shown.
New dependency beside the tower replaced the 1831 provision store; it could also house survivors.
Tower clapboarded to make it watertight (LighthouseFriends).
Cannon installed as the first sound signal at the point (register); fired hourly in fog and snow (LighthouseFriends).
Two red horizontal stripes added to the day-mark (LighthouseFriends).
Flag signal system and telegraph added to the station (LighthouseFriends).
Keeper's dwelling built 1911-1912, attached to the tower (register; Corporation's history).
Triple-flashing catoptric apparatus replaced the original lighting apparatus (LighthouseFriends).
Three-inch diaphone foghorn in a fog-signal building 1.2 miles south-west of the lighthouse (LighthouseFriends). The 1919 report lists new fog-alarm plants at Pointe des Monts.
HMCS Magog torpedoed by U-1223 off Pointe-des-Monts, 14 October 1944, while escorting convoy GONS.33.
Historic tower's light last exhibited on 4 December 1964; the function passed to a skeletal tower at the second site.

Classified as a heritage immovable on 8 September 1965 (register). The Corporation's keepers' page says the Ministry of Cultural Affairs agreed to classify it in 1964; the Corporation's history page says 1965.
Government of Quebec bought the lighthouse (LighthouseFriends).
Fog signal deactivated (LighthouseFriends).
Light on the skeletal tower at the second site automated; last keeper transferred (LighthouseFriends).
Management of the site entrusted to a non-profit corporation drawn from local and regional bodies.
Replacement light on the skeletal tower deactivated; its tower removed (LighthouseFriends).
Skeletal tower at the second site removed (LighthouseFriends).
Thorough restoration of the dwellings and refreshed exhibits in the tower (LighthouseFriends).

keepers.name: James Wallace
keepers.note: First keeper. LighthouseFriends says he served fourteen years.

keepers.name: Zoël Bédard
keepers.note: Spelled 'Zoël Bedard' by LighthouseFriends. Died in office in 1867; his body was kept at the station for six months.

keepers.name: Paul Peuliot
keepers.note: Spelled 'Pouliot' by the Corporation's site. Former sea captain; an inspector in 1872 found him unwell and he was removed.

keepers.name: Louis-Ferdinand Fafard
keepers.note: Named 'Louis-F. Fafard' in the French list. His two eldest sons tended the light during his six months' leave.

keepers.name: Victor Fafard
keepers.note: Keepers' table (Marine report printed 1916, scan p. 82, printed p. 75) prints 'V. Faffard' against the station, appointed July 10, 1889, salary 880.00. Image checked: the row reads 'Monts, Pointe des, light and explosive fog signal | V. Faffard | July 10, 1889 | 880 00'. The printed surname has a double f; the link to Victor Fafard rests on the station and the 1889 date. Died in February 1926; twelve children (Corporation's page).

keepers.name: Georges Fafard
keepers.note: Left in 1954 for Mitis-sur-Mer. Wife Alphonsia Fafard described the 1944 convoy escort.

keepers.name: Sauveur Duguay
keepers.note: Public role only. Named by the Corporation and LighthouseFriends.

keepers.name: Jacques Landry
keepers.note: Public role only: named by the Corporation as the keeper whose efforts, with others, saved the old tower from demolition.

wrecks.outcome: Stranded at Point des Monts; causes formally investigated at Quebec City.
Stranded near Pointe des Monts; formal investigation at Montreal on 29 May. Year inferred from the report's fiscal year ended 31 March 1919.
Stranded near Pointe des Monts; preliminary inquiry at Quebec on 20 November. Year inferred from the fiscal year ended 31 March 1920.
Torpedoed by U-1223 off Pointe-des-Monts while escorting convoy GONS.33; towed to Quebec and declared a constructive total loss. LighthouseFriends gives three sailors killed.

corrections.why: The historic tower's light was last exhibited on 4 December 1964 and passed to a skeletal tower at the second site (LighthouseFriends; register 92571). The 2000 date belongs to the replacement light on the skeletal tower, which was deactivated and its tower removed that year.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: LighthouseFriends gives the whole tower as 90 ft (27 m). The Corporation's site gives 21 m (69 ft) as the height of the viewing level above ground. Both figures are kept in the story: the tower to the top and the level visitors reach.

The Corporation's history says the Ministry agreed in 1964 to classify the tower and powder magazine; the Quebec register gives 8 September 1965 as the ministerial date. Both dates appear in the story.

notes_for_editor: Disagreements left open, all stated in the story: Fafard years 82 (Corporation) vs 83 (LighthouseFriends); tower height 27 m (LighthouseFriends, whole tower) vs 21 m (Corporation, viewing level); Magog stern loss 60 ft (Navy) vs 65 ft (LighthouseFriends); keeper's name 'Peuliot' (LighthouseFriends) vs 'Pouliot' (Corporation); protection dates 1964 (Corporation keepers' page) vs 1965 (Corporation history page and register 92571, 8 Sept 1965). Matched by position on OCR: the 1916 keepers' table row for Pointe des Monts is printed 'V. Faffard' (double f); the page image (scan p. 82, printed p. 75) was checked and confirms the row, the date (10 July 1889) and the salary (880.00). The story says the link to Victor Fafard rests on the station and date. Fiscal years: Marine reports are labelled by fiscal year end (volume printed 1920 = year ended 31 March 1919; printed 1921 = year ended 31 March 1920). The May 1918 and November 1919 strandings are dated by that inference; the vessels are not named in the entries read. The 1918 fog-alarm date is LighthouseFriends' only; the 1919 report lists new fog-alarm plants including Pointe des Monts for the year ended 31 March 1919 without a month. The Sardhana entry (19 July 1903) is in the volume printed 1904 (Thirty-Sixth Annual Report, 1903); the entry carries its own date. The court's finding that the fog signal was inefficient is from the same entry. The 1830 first-light date is in both LighthouseFriends and register 92571. The 1830 cost (£4,727) and the Lampson and Bayfield episodes are LighthouseFriends only. The 1873 schooner, 1883 telegraph, 1928 wireless and 1914 apparatus are LighthouseFriends only (community site; facts only). Living-person rule: Landry (service ended 1978) and Boudreault (1978-1983) are named in public role only, from the Corporation's page and LighthouseFriends' roster; the Corporation's note that Landry is now a mayor is not used. Duguay and Georges Fafard ended service before 1960. Alphonsia Fafard appears only as LighthouseFriends prints her account (1944). The register says the keeper's house dates 1911-1912 and that the tower has seven levels; the Corporation's record 9366 also says six floors of stairs; the story follows register 92571 and the Corporation. Wikipedia (FR) keeper list was seen only as a lead and is not cited. No Quebec newspaper search was run (BAnQ not used).
